info.title: OpenAI Compatible API
info.description:
Scaleway Generative APIs provides access to the latest AI models hosted on Scaleway infrastructure.

The Generative APIs specification targets OpenAI API compatibility.

For details about the Scaleway Generative APIs used for dedicated deployments, refer to the [Generative APIs - Dedicated Deployment API](https://www.scaleway.com/en/developers/api/inference) documentation.

## Concepts

Refer to the [dedicated concepts page](https://www.scaleway.com/en/docs/generative-apis/concepts/) to find definitions of the different terms referring to Generative APIs.

## Quickstart

<Message type="requirement">
To complete the actions presented below, you must have:
  - A Scaleway account logged in to the [console](https://console.scaleway.com/organization)
  - A valid [API key](https://www.scaleway.com/en/docs/iam/how-to/create-api-keys/) with sufficient [IAM permissions](https://www.scaleway.com/en/docs/iam/reference-content/permission-sets/) to perform the actions described on this page
  - [Installed `curl`](https://curl.se/download.html)
</Message>

1. (Optional) Configure your environment variables to simplify your usage of the APIs.

    ```bash
    export SCW_ACCESS_KEY="<API access key>"
    export SCW_SECRET_KEY="<API secret key>"
    export SCW_REGION="<Scaleway region>"
    ```
2. Generate content from a model by running the following command.
    ```bash
    curl https://api.scaleway.ai/v1/chat/completions \
      -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
      -H "Authorization: Bearer $SCW_SECRET_KEY" \
      -d '{
        "model": "llama-3.3-70b-instruct",
        "messages": [
          {
            "role": "system",
            "content": "You are a helpful assistant."
          },
          {
            "role": "user",
            "content": "Hello!"
          }
        ]
      }'
    ```

See [How to use Generative APIs](https://www.scaleway.com/en/docs/generative-apis/how-to/)
for quickstart information and snippets using `REST` requests or libraries such as the `openai` Python client.


## Technical information

### Regions

Scaleway's infrastructure is spread across different [regions and Availability Zones](https://www.scaleway.com/en/docs/account/reference-content/products-availability/).

Generative APIs is available in the Paris region, which is represented by the following path parameter (optional while there is only one region):
- `fr-par`

### Supported endpoints and features

Supported endpoints are:
- `/v1/responses`
- `/v1/chat/completions`
- `/v1/audio/transcriptions`
- `/v1/embeddings`
- `/v1/rerank`
- `/v1/batches`
- `/v1/models`

The `/v1/chat/completions` endpoint:
- **Supported features**:
  - Structured outputs (JSON response format)
  - Tool calling (i.e., compatibility with workflows using MCP servers)
  - Sending and analyzing images
  - Sending and analyzing audio files
- **Not supported parameters**: `audio`, `metadata`, `modalities`,
`prediction`, `prompt_cache_key`, `user`, `safety_identifier`,
`service_tier`, `stream_options.include_obfuscation`, `store`, `system_fingerprint`,
`web_search_options`
- **Not supported tools**: only `function` tools are supported. `custom` tools require you to provide a custom `grammar` to verify their input format

The `/v1/audio/transcriptions` endpoint:
- **Not supported parameters**: `chunking_strategy`, `include[]` and `timestamp_granularities[]`

The `/v1/responses` endpoint:
- **Supported features**: currently, only `function` tools are supported. These tools must be fully defined in your query, and should be executed if the model requests them. The execution result is then sent to the model so that it can use this additional context to produce a suitable answer.
- **Not supported features**: 
  - storing conversation state server-side 
  - execution by Scaleway of "built-in" tools (such as web or file search) while the model generates a response
  - sending response output object directly as an input for the next message. Standard messages using `role:assistant` and `content` fields should be used instead. Specifically, `custom_tool_call` and `custom_tool_call_output` types are not yet supported. As a workaround, tool call results can be sent using `role:user`, although Scaleway recommends using `/chat/completions` for better results in this case.
- **Not supported parameters**: `background`, `conversation`, `include`,
`instructions`, `max_tool_calls`, `metadata`, `previous_response_id`, `prompt_cache_key`,
`safety_identifier`, `service_tier`, `stream_options`, `top_logprobs`, `user`, `prompt`, `verbosity`

The `/v1/batches` endpoint:
- **Supported features**: processing files stored in Object Storage (using the Amazon S3 protocol)
- **Not supported parameters**: `metadata`

The `/v1/rerank` endpoint:
- **Compatiblity**: aims for compatibility with the JinAI API and Cohere API formats (no OpenAI API exists for this endpoint)

### Third-party tool integration

For full details of direct integration into third party tooling, see [Integrating Scaleway Generative APIs with popular AI tools](https://www.scaleway.com/en/docs/generative-apis/reference-content/integrating-generative-apis-with-popular-tools/).
If your tool is not listed, you can still specify the Scaleway URL and
API key in most OpenAI-like plugins, as compatibility largely depends on the above APIs.

## Technical limitations

When choosing a model, select the ones compatible with the API endpoints you want to use
in the [model catalog](https://www.scaleway.com/en/docs/generative-apis/reference-content/supported-models/).
For example, `/v1/embeddings` is only available for embeddings models.

## Going further

For more information about Generative APIs, you can check out the following pages:

* [Generative APIs Documentation](https://www.scaleway.com/en/docs/generative-apis/)
* [Generative APIs FAQ](https://www.scaleway.com/en/docs/generative-apis/faq/)
* [Scaleway Slack Community - AI Channel](https://scaleway-community.slack.com/archives/C01SGLGRLEA) join the #ai channel
* [Contact Scaleway support](https://console.scaleway.com/support/tickets)

## Troubleshooting

See [Troubleshooting Generative APIs](https://www.scaleway.com/en/docs/generative-apis/troubleshooting/)
for descriptions regarding advanced API behavior and solutions to common issues.

tags.name: Chat Completions
tags.description: A chat completion is a model response for a given conversation. It represents the functionality of generating a response in a chat context

tags.name: Responses
tags.description: A response is a model output for a given input. It represents the functionality of generating a response in various contexts.

tags.name: Embeddings
tags.description:
A vector representation of an input.
Similar vectors corresponds to semantically similar inputs.

See [How to query embedding models](https://www.scaleway.com/en/docs/generative-apis/how-to/query-embedding-models/)
for code snippets using `openai` Python client.

tags.name: Rerank
tags.description:
A ranking is an ordering of documents by relevance, based on a query.

See [How to query reranking models](https://www.scaleway.com/en/docs/generative-apis/how-to/query-reranking-models/)
for code snippets using `openai` Python client.

tags.name: Audio
tags.description:
A transcription is a text transcribed from an audio input.

To support file upload, this API must be queried with `multipart/form-data` content type instead of `application/json`.

See [How to query audio models](https://www.scaleway.com/en/docs/generative-apis/how-to/query-audio-models/)
for code snippets using `openai` Python client.

tags.name: Batch
tags.description:
A batch is an asynchronous process that executes multiple requests. It takes a file containing the requests to perform
 as input, and writes the results to an output file.

Files are stored within Scaleway Object Storage.

See [How to use batch processing](https://www.scaleway.com/en/docs/generative-apis/how-to/use-batch-processing/)
for code snippets using `openai` Python client.

tags.name: Models
tags.description: A model refers to a system that has been trained to generate content such as text, images, or other data types based on input prompts or instructions

detail.description: Detail level of the image provided to the model.

image_url.description:
URL of a remote image or encoding in base64 of a local image.

See [How to query vision models](https://www.scaleway.com/en/docs/generative-apis/how-to/query-vision-models/)
for code snippets using the `openai` Python client, and guidance for encoding local images.

content​.description:
List of input contents of different `type`, each compatible with different fields:

`input_text`: Requires `text` field.

`input_image`: Requires `detail` and `image_url` fields.

`input_file`: Requires `file_data` or `file_url` field. Optionally, `filename` can be provided.

type.description: Type of the content input. Always set to `message`.
Type of content. Always set to `output_text`.

annotations.description: Annotations of the text output, such as citations or path to a file.

role.description: Role generating the content output. Always set to `assistant`.

type.description:
List of outputs of different `type`, each also outputting different fields:

`message`: outputs `content` field

`function_call`: outputs `call_id`, `name` and `arguments` fields

id.description: UUID of the mesage within a response.

call_id.description: UUID of the function tool call.

arguments.description:
Arguments to pass to the function, formatted as a JSON string.

Example: `{"city": "Paris","timezone": "UTC+2"}`

input_tokens_details.description: Breakdown of input tokens by type.

output_tokens_details.description: Breakdown of output tokens by type.

reasoning_tokens.description: Number of output tokens used for reasoning.

total_tokens.description: Total number of tokens (input and output).

type.description: Type of tool call, always set to `function`.

function.description: Function to call, identified by the model.

name.description: Name of the function to call.

arguments.description: Arguments to call the function with, as generated by the model in JSON format. Note that model may not always generate valid JSON or parameters. Validate the arguments in your code before calling a function.

ChatCompletionMessageToolCalls.description: List of tool calls required by the model, such as function calls.

type.description: Type of content. `image_url` and `input_audio` are only supported with `user` role.

text.description: Text content. Required if `type` is set to `text`.

url.description:
URL of a remote image or encoding in base64 of a local image. Required if `type` is set to `image_url`.

See [How to query vision models](https://www.scaleway.com/en/docs/generative-apis/how-to/query-vision-models/)
for code snippets using `openai` Python client or how to encode local images.

data.description:
Encoding in base64 of a local audio file. Required if `type` is set to `input_audio`.

See [How to query audio models](https://www.scaleway.com/en/docs/generative-apis/how-to/query-audio-models/)
for code snippets using `openai` Python client or how to encode local audio files.

format.description: Format of the encoded audio file. Currently, the only supported values are `wav` and `mp3`.

content.description: Content of a message as string. Required for all roles, except `assistant` if `tool_calls` is specified instead.

content​.description: Content of a message as array of content parts. Required for all roles, except `assistant` if `tool_calls` is specified instead.

tool_calls.description: List of tool calls required by the model. Can only be used with `assistant` if `content` is not specified.

tool_call_id.description: UUID of the tool call. Must only be used with `tool` role.

role.description: Role of the message's author, always set to `assistant` in the response.

reasoning_content.description: Reasoning content generated for this message.

ChatCompletionStreamOptions.description: An object containing parameters that modify the behavior of stream responses. Can only be used if `stream` is set to `true`.

include_usage.description: Defines whether a usage field is included in a stream. If set, an additional chunk will be streamed before the `data: [DONE]` message. The `usage` field on this chunk shows the token usage statistics for the complete stream.

logprob.description: Log probability of generating this token, if it is among the top 20 most likely tokens. Otherwise, the value `-9999.0` is used to mean that the token is very unlikely.

bytes.description: List of integers representing the UTF-8 bytes (in decimal format) representation of a token. Since some characters may be represented by multiple tokens, this representation can be combined to represent the corresponding character in UTF-8.

top_logprobs.description: List of most probable next tokens and their log probability.

token.description: A token among the most next likely ones.

logprob.description: Log probability of generating this token, if it is among the top 20 most likely tokens. Otherwise, the value `-9999.0` will be used to mean that the token is very unlikely.

bytes.description: List of integers representing the UTF-8 bytes (in decimal format) representation of a token. Since some characters may be represented by multiple tokens, this representation can be combined to represent the corresponding character in UTF-8.

type.description: Type of tool object, always set to `function`.

ChatCompletionToolChoiceOption.description:
Defines whether a model can call tools, and if so, and which ones.

`none`: model will not call any tools, and only generate a message.

`auto`: model can choose either to generate a message, or to call one or
multiple tools.

`required`: model must call one or multiple tools.

Default: `none` when no tools are present, otherwise `auto`.

An object can also be provided to specify a tool that the model
must call. Object format must be:

`{"type": "function", "function": {"name": "function_name_as_provided_in_tools"}}`

index.description: Index of the choice in the list of choices.

logprobs.description: Object containing log probability information for each token in a generated response.

content.description: List of content tokens and their log probability information.

refusal.description: List of refusal tokens and their log probability information.

finish_reason.description:
Reason the model stopped generating tokens.

`stop`: model successfully reached the end of its answer, or a provided
stop sequence

`length`: maximum number of output tokens was reached, blocking further generation

`tool_calls`: model needed to call a tool

total_tokens.description: Total number of tokens (input and output).

completion_tokens_details.description: Breakdown of output tokens by type.

reasoning_tokens.description: Number of output tokens used for reasoning.

prompt_tokens_details.description: Breakdown of input tokens by type.

object.description: Type of response object, always set to `chat.completion`.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the response was generated (Unix format, in seconds).

output.description: List of outputs generated by the model as response.

text.description: Configuration of the response format, either plain text or JSON structured data.

object.description: Type of response object, always set to `chat.completion`.

created.description: Timestamp when the response was generated (Unix format, in seconds).

choices.description: List of chat completion variations. Defaults to only `1` choice, but can be increased by setting a value for `n` in the request.

object.description: Type of response object, always set to `list`.

created.description: Timestamp when the response was generated (Unix format, in seconds).

usage.description: Usage information generated by this request.

total_tokens.description: Total number of tokens (input and output).

completion_tokens.description: Number of output tokens. Always set to `0` for embedding models since no token are generated (only vectors coordinates).

index.description: Index of the embedding in the list of embeddings.

object.description: Type of the response object, always set to `embedding`.

embedding.description: Embedding vector, represented as a list of floating point values. The length of a vector is equal to the number of dimensions of the model.

results.description: List of documents sorted by relevance.

usage.description: Usage information generated by this request.

total_tokens.description: Total number of tokens (reranking models only use input tokens).

index.description: Index of the document in the initial request.

relevance_score.description: Document's relevance to answering the query.

usage.description:
Usage information generated by this request, either in tokens or duration depending
on how the model is billed.

type.description: Usage type for this model. Either `duration` or `tokens`.

object.description: Type of batch object, always set to `batch`.

endpoint.description: Path used to process requests in the batch.

model.description: Model used to process the batch

object.description: Type of batch object, always set to `list`.

line.description: Line number in the file where error occured

param.description: Name of the parameter that triggered error, if applicable

completion_window.description: Time range during which the batch should be processed.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the batch was created (Unix format, in seconds).

in_progress_at.description: Timestamp when the batch processing started (Unix format, in seconds).

expires_at.description: Timestamp when the batch will expire (Unix format, in seconds).

finalizing_at.description: Timestamp when the batch started finalizing (Unix format, in seconds).

completed_at.description: Timestamp when the batch was completed (Unix format, in seconds).

failed_at.description: Timestamp when the batch failed (Unix format, in seconds).

expired_at.description: Timestamp when the batch expired (Unix format, in seconds).

cancelling_at.description: Timestamp when the batch started cancelling (Unix format, in seconds).

cancelled_at.description: Timestamp when the batch was cancelled (Unix format, in seconds).

usage.description:
Usage information generated by the requests of the batch, either in tokens or duration depending
on how the model is billed.

type.description: Usage type for this model. Either `duration` or `tokens`.

input_tokens_details.description: A detailed breakdown of the input tokens.

cached_tokens.description: Number of tokens that were retrieved from the cache.

total_tokens.description: Total number of tokens (input and output).

output_tokens.description: Number of output tokens. Always set to `0` for embedding models since no token are generated (only vector coordinates).

output_tokens_details.description: A detailed breakdown of the output tokens.

object.description: Type of response object, always set to `list`.

first_id.description: UUID of first batch in the response.

last_id.description: UUID of last batch in the response.

has_more.description: Defines whether there are more results to retrieve not returned by this query.

type.description: Type of tool object, always set to `function`.

name.description: Name of the function to be called. Must contain only `a-z`, `A-Z`, `0-9`, underscores and dashes, with a maximum length of `64` characters.

description.description: Description of the function. This helps the model choose the right function when needed.

strict.description:
Defines whether to enforce strict schema adherence when generating a
function call. If set to `true`, the model will follow the exact
schema defined in the `parameters` field. Currently, even if
set `true` this parameter will be ignored and act as if set to `false`.
We recommend you check output schema before calling any functions or tools.

**Default:** `false`

description.description: Description of the function. This helps the model choose the right function when needed.

name.description: Name of the function to be called. Must contain only `a-z`, `A-Z`, `0-9`, underscores and dashes, with a maximum length of `64` characters.

strict.description:
Defines whether to enforce strict schema adherence when generating a
function call. If set to `true`, the model will follow the exact
schema defined in the `parameters` field. Currently, even if
set `true` this parameter will be ignored and act as if set to `false`.
We recommend you check output schema before calling any functions or tools.

**Default:** `false`

FunctionParameters.description:
Parameters of the function, described as a JSON schema object. See [How to use function calling](https://www.scaleway.com/en/docs/generative-apis/how-to/use-function-calling/) for examples, and the [JSON schema reference](https://json-schema.org/understanding-json-schema/) for documentation about the format.
Omitting `parameters` defines a function with an empty parameter list.

object.description: Type of response object, always set to `list`.

created.description: Timestamp when the model was created (Unix format, in seconds).

owned_by.description: Name of the organization that created the model (i.e. the model provider).

ParallelToolCalls.description:
Defines whether the model can call multiple tools. Currently, even if
set `false` this parameter will be ignored and act as if set to `true`.

Only [specific models](https://www.scaleway.com/en/docs/managed-inference/reference-content/model-catalog/#model-details)
can call multiple tools in a single response.

**Default value:** `true`

MaxOutputTokens.description:
Maximum number of output tokens that can be generated
for a `completion`.
Different [default maximum values](https://www.scaleway.com/en/docs/generative-apis/reference-content/supported-models/)
are enforced for each model, to avoid edge cases where tokens are
generated indefinitely. These values are not enforced
in [Managed Inference](https://www.scaleway.com/en/inference/).

ResponseFormatChatCompletion.description:
Output format specification.

Using `{ "type": "json_schema", "json_schema": {...} }`
enables the model to output only a valid JSON following the provided schema specification.

Deprecated. Using `{ "type": "json_object" }` enables `JSON
mode` that should not be used anymore.

See [How to use structured outputs](https://www.scaleway.com/en/docs/generative-apis/how-to/use-structured-outputs/)
for code snippets using `openai` Python client and the [JSON Schema reference](https://json-schema.org/understanding-json-schema/)
for documentation about the format.

json_schema.description:
Schema the response object should follow in `JSON` format. This field
can only be used if `type` is set to `json_schema`.

ResponseFormatResponseAPI.description:
Output format specification.

Using `{ "type": "text"}` ensures the model enables output text (default behavior).

Using `{ "type": "json_schema", "name": ..., "schema": {...}, "description": ...,"strict": true}`
enables the model to output only valid JSON following the provided schema specification.

Deprecated. Using `{ "type": "json_object" }` enables `JSON
mode`, and should no longer be used.

See [How to use structured outputs](https://www.scaleway.com/en/docs/generative-apis/how-to/use-structured-outputs/)
for code snippets using the `openai` Python client, and the [JSON Schema reference](https://json-schema.org/understanding-json-schema/)
for documentation about the format.

type.description:
Type of response object. The properties `name`, `schema`, `description` and `strict`
can only be used if `type` is set to `json_schema`.

name.description: Name of the response format. Must only contain alphanumeric characters, underscores and dashes.

description.description:
Description of the response format. This helps the model
generate a response that follows the desired structure.

schema.description:
Schema the response object should follow in `JSON` format. This field
can only be used if `type` is set to `json_schema`. [Learn more](https://www.scaleway.com/en/docs/generative-apis/how-to/use-structured-outputs/)

strict.description:
Defines whether to enforce strict schema adherence when generating
structured output. Currently, only `true` is supported.

**Default:** `true`

StopConfiguration.description:
String, or array of strings, that when encountered in the generated text
will stop the model from generating further output tokens.
The generated text will not return any of the specified stop sequences.
A maximum of 4 sequences can be provided.

Temperature.description:
Value between `0` and `2` which increases randomness in token generation (e.g. encourages content "creativity" instead of "predictability").

`temperature:0` means the distribution learned by the model will be used directly, favoring a subset of the most probable tokens at each generation step.

`temperature>0` means randomness is added to the learnt distribution, so that tokens with a lower probability can also be generated.

`temperature>=1` means added randomness will be so high, that almost all tokens are equally probable, leading the model to potentially mix languages.

The ideal `temperature` value depends on the use case and model. We recommend setting `temperature` to the recommended value for each model,
as shown in Console Playground (these values are used by default).

Note that `temperature` does not affect request reproducibility (only affected by the `seed` parameter).
With the same `seed` and `temperature`, two identical requests to a model will generate the same response.

TopP.description:
Value between `0` and `1` which increases the proportion of token vocabulary considered during generation (`0` cannot be used).

`top_p`:`0.9` means the next token will be chosen from the 90% most probable tokens at each generation step.

We recommend setting `top_p` to the recommended value for each model, as shown in Console Playground (these values are used by default).

ProjectId.description:
The ID of the Project you want to target. If this value is not provided,
your default Project will be used.

Specifying this value allows you to limit access through IAM policies,
or to allocate consumption and billing to a specific project.

post.description:
Create a model response for a given input.
This method accepts a sequence of messages (a chat conversation) and returns a response generated by the model.

Currently, this API **does not store** inputs and `store` is set to `false` even if not provided.

input.description: String or list of inputs to provide to the model to generate a response. Use an array of inputs to provide multiple strings and/or other content types.

model.description:
Unique identifier of the model. For now, the Responses API only supports `gpt-oss-120b`.

Refer to our [supported models](https://www.scaleway.com/en/docs/generative-apis/reference-content/supported-models/) list
or [/models](#path-models-list-models) endpoint for available models.

instructions.description: System message added to the model's context.

effort.description:
Reasoning effort level to generate the response.
`minimal` is currently not supported.

store.description:
Defines whether to store the input content for future requests.
`store` is currently not supported and always set to `false`.

stream.description:
Defines whether the model's response can be streamed to the client
using server-sent events.

The response will be streamed in chunks over HTTP, where each chunk except
the last contains the following content:

`data: {"id": ..., "model": ..., "output":...}`

The last chunk will contain `data: [DONE]`.

Note that the object `{"id": ..., "model": ..., "output":...}` follows the same format as
a non-stream HTTP request.

See [How to query language models using streaming](https://www.scaleway.com/en/docs/generative-apis/how-to/query-language-models/#streaming)
for examples, and [server-sent events](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Server-sent_events/Using_server-sent_events)
for reference documentation about SSE format.

**Default value:** `false`

text.description: Configuration of the response format, either plain text or JSON structured data.

tools.description: List of tools the model can call, such as functions. A maximum of `128` tools can be provided. See [How to use function calling](https://www.scaleway.com/en/docs/generative-apis/how-to/use-function-calling/) for code snippets using the `openai` Python client.

top_logprobs.description:
Number of most likely tokens to return for each token generated, along with their
generation log probability.
Value must be between `0` and `20`.
`logprobs` must be set to `true` to use this parameter.

truncation.description:
Truncation configuration for the model response.
Only `disabled` is currently supported.

post.description:
Create a model response for a given chat conversation.
This method accepts a sequence of messages (a chat conversation) and returns a response generated by the model.

Conversation `messages` **are not stored** and need to be sent in each
`/chat/completions` API call.

model.description:
Unique identifier of the model, such as `llama-3.3-70b-instruct` or `mistral-small-3.2-24b-instruct-2506`.

Refer to our [supported models](https://www.scaleway.com/en/docs/generative-apis/reference-content/supported-models/) list
or [/models](#path-models-list-models) endpoint for available models.

messages.description: Array of messages representing the conversation history.

max_tokens.description:
Use `max_completion_tokens` instead. Maximum number of total tokens that can be generated
for a completion (input and output).

frequency_penalty.description:
Value which influences the likelihood of generating tokens based on their frequency in the existing text.
When set to a positive value, it reduces the probability of repeating tokens that have already appeared.

logit_bias.description:
List of token IDs with associated bias integer values ranging from `-100` to `100`. This parameter adjusts the probability of these tokens being generated during the model's output.
A JSON object must be provided in the following format: `{"354": 80,"143": -50}` where `354` and `143` are token IDs from the tokenizer used with this model. Positive values increase the likelihood of a token being generated, while negative values reduce it.
Model `qwen3.5-397b-a17b` does not support this field.

logprobs.description:
Defines whether to return log probabilities of each output token.
This allows you to see the likelihood of each token being generated.

n.description:
Number of chat completion choices to generate for a given input.
The value of `n` multiplies the number of generated tokens,
resulting in `n` separate responses for each input.

presence_penalty.description:
Value which influences the probability of generating tokens that have
already appeared in the text. Positive values reduce the likelihood of
repeating a token, regardless of how many times it has already appeared.

reasoning_effort.description:
Reasoning effort level to generate the response.

For `qwen3.5-397b-a17b` and `qwen3.6-35b-a3b` model:
  - `low` and `high` values are similar to `medium`

For `mistral-medium-3.5-128b` model:
  - `low` and `medium` values are not supported

For `gpt-oss-120b` model:
  - `none` value is not supported

seed.description:
Value which controls the randomness of the output to ensure determinism.
When using the same seed value along with identical input and parameters,
you should receive the same model response each time. This holds true even when
temperature is set above 0.

Note that fully deterministic output is not guaranteed over long periods of time (such
as several months), as the inference model may be updated and optimized.

stream.description:
Defines whether the model's response can be streamed to the client
using server-sent events.

The response will be streamed in chunks over HTTP, where each chunk except
the last contains the following content:

`data: {"id": ..., "model": ..., "choices":...}`

The last chunk will contain `data: [DONE]`.

Note that the object `{"id": ..., "model": ..., "choices":...}` follows the same format as
a non-stream HTTP request.

See [How to query language models using streaming](https://www.scaleway.com/en/docs/generative-apis/how-to/query-language-models/#streaming)
for examples, and [server-sent events](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Server-sent_events/Using_server-sent_events)
for reference documentation about SSE format.

**Default value:** `false`

tools.description: List of tools the model can call, such as functions. A maximum of `128` tools can be provided. See [How to use function calling](https://www.scaleway.com/en/docs/generative-apis/how-to/use-function-calling/) for code snippets using `openai` Python client.

top_logprobs.description:
Number of most likely tokens to return for each token generated, along with their
generation log probability.
Value must be between `0` and `20`.
`logprobs` must be set to `true` to use this parameter.

input.description:
String or Array of strings to represent as embedding vector.
Maximum array items: `2048`

model.description:
Unique identifier of the model, such as `bge-multilingual-gemma2`.
Refer to our [supported models](https://www.scaleway.com/en/docs/generative-apis/reference-content/supported-models/) list or [/models](#path-models-list-models) endpoint for available models.

dimensions.description: Number of `dimensions` to use for the embedding vector representation. Currently, the only supported value is that of the [maximum dimensions of a model](https://www.scaleway.com/en/docs/generative-apis/reference-content/supported-models/#embedding-models). Lower values are not supported and vectors should not be trimmed, since available models do not support [matryoshka embeddings](https://huggingface.co/blog/matryoshka).

x-codeSamples.source:
curl https://api.scaleway.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SCW_SECRET_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "input": "Here is a text to embed as a vector",
    "model": "bge-multilingual-gemma2"
  }'

post.description: Identify most relevant documents to answer a query.

query.description: Query requiring relevant documents to provide a better answer.

documents.description:
Array of document contents in string format.
Maximum array items: `1000`

model.description:
Unique identifier of the model, such as `qwen3-embedding-8b`.
Refer to our [supported models](https://www.scaleway.com/en/docs/generative-apis/reference-content/supported-models/) list or [/models](#path-models-list-models) endpoint for available models.

top_n.description: Number of most relevant documents to retrieve.

x-codeSamples.source:
curl https://api.scaleway.ai/v1/rerank \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SCW_SECRET_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "qwen3-embedding-8b",
    "query": "What is the biggest area of water on earth ?",
    "documents": [
      "The Pacific is approximately 165 million km²",
      "Oceans can be sorted by size: Pacific, Atlantic, Indian",
      "The Atlantic is a very large ocean.",
      "The deepest pool on earth is 96 000 m²"
    ],
    "top_n": 3
  }'

file.description:
Audio file object to transcribe. Currently, the only supported formats are `wav`, `mp3`, `flac`, `mpga`, `oga`, `ogg`.

See [How to query audio models](https://www.scaleway.com/en/docs/generative-apis/how-to/query-audio-models/)
for code snippets using `openai` Python client.

model.description:
Unique identifier of the model, such as `whisper-large-v3`.
Refer to our [supported models](https://www.scaleway.com/en/docs/generative-apis/reference-content/supported-models/) list or [/models](#path-models-list-models) endpoint for available models.

language.description:
Language of the audio input, following [ISO-639-1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_ISO_639_language_codes) format such as `en` for English.
Refer to our [model catalog](https://www.scaleway.com/en/docs/managed-inference/reference-content/model-catalog/)
for supported languages.

**Default**: Language will be automatically detected if no value is provided.

prompt.description:
Additional content used to guide the model during transcription.
This fields works very differently from prompts in `/chat/completions`.
Refer to [How to query audio models](https://www.scaleway.com/en/docs/generative-apis/how-to/query-audio-models/)
for more information.

response_format.description: Output format structure. Currently, the only supported value is `json`.

stream.description:
Defines whether the model's response can be streamed to the client
using server-sent events.

The response will be streamed in chunks over HTTP, where each chunk except
the last contains the following content:

`data: {"type": ..., "delta": ..., "logprobs":...}`

The last chunk will contain `data: [DONE]`.

Note that the object `data: {"type": ..., "delta": ..., "logprobs":...}` does not follow the same format as
a non-stream HTTP request.

See [How to query audio models using streaming](https://www.scaleway.com/en/docs/generative-apis/how-to/query-audio-models/#streaming)
for examples, and [server-sent events](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Server-sent_events/Using_server-sent_events)
for reference documentation about SSE format.

**Default value:** `false`

get.description: List batches including their properties and status.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description:
Pagination cursor which value should be a batch UUID. When response consists of
multiple pages, provide the last batch UUID obtained in previous request to fetch next page.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of batches to retrieve.

post.description: Process multiple requests asynchronously in batch.

completion_window.description: Time range during which the batch should be processed. Currently only `24h` is supported.

endpoint.description:
Path to use to process requests in the batch. Currently `/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/responses`,
`/v1/embeddings` and `/v1/audio/transcriptions` are supported.

input_file_id.description:
URL of the file in Scaleway Object Storage. File should contain all request to process in [JSONL format](https://jsonlines.org/).
Results will be stored within the same bucket and folder, and named `{filename}-output.jsonl` and `{filename}-error.jsonl`.

See [How to use batch processing](https://www.scaleway.com/en/docs/generative-apis/how-to/use-batch-processing/)
for code snippets using `openai` Python client.

output_expires_after.description: Expiration rules for the output and error files generated by the batch.

anchor.description: Reference timestamp after which the expiration duration applies. Supported value: `created_at`

seconds.description: Number of seconds after anchor timestamp that the file will expire. Value must be between 3600 (1 hour) and 31 536 000 (1 year).

get.description: Retrieve a batch's properties and status.

delete.description:
Delete a previously created batch.

When a batch is deleted, the associated `input.jsonl`, `output.jsonl` and `errors.jsonl` files are not removed from the bucket.

This endpoint is a Scaleway‑specific extension that supplements the OpenAI‑compatible API; it is not part of the official OpenAI API specification.

post.description:
When a batch is cancelled, results already processed are stored
in corresponding `output.jsonl` and `errors.jsonl` files, while remaining
requests will not be processed.

get.description: List [models](https://www.scaleway.com/en/docs/generative-apis/reference-content/supported-models/) that are available via this API.
